'''Aizik Isaakovich Vol'pert''' ({{langx|ru|Айзик Исаакович Вольперт}}; 5 June 1923<ref name="biobib"/><ref name="biobib2"/> – January 2006) (the family name is also transliterated as '''[[Volpert]]'''<ref>See {{harvtxt|Chuyko|2009|p=79}}.</ref> or '''Wolpert'''<ref name="Miklhin 1986 369">See {{harvnb|Mikhlin|Prössdorf|1986|p=369}}.</ref>) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and [[Israel]]i [[mathematician]] and [[chemical engineer]]<ref>His training as an engineer is clearly indicated by {{harvtxt|Truesdell|1991|p=88, footnote 1}} who, referring to the book {{Harv|Hudjaev|Vol'pert|1985}}, writes exactly:-"''Be it noted that this clear, excellent, and compact book is written by and for engineers''".</ref> working in [[partial differential equation]]s, [[Bounded variation|functions of bounded variation]] and [[chemical kinetics]].

== Life and academic career==
Vol'pert graduated from [[Lviv University]] in 1951, earning the [[candidate of science]] degree and the [[Docent#Central and Eastern Europe|docent]] title respectively in 1954 and 1956 from the same university:<ref name="biobib"/> from 1951 on he worked at the [[Ukrainian National Forestry University|Lviv Industrial Forestry Institute]].<ref name="biobib"/> In 1961 he became [[Research fellow#Russian Federation|senior research fellow]]<ref>Precisely he became "''старший научный сотрудник''", abbreviated as "''ст. науч. сотр.''", according to {{harvtxt|Fomin|Shilov|1969|p=265}}.</ref> while 1962 he earned the "[[doktor nauk]]"<ref name="biobib2"/> degree from [[Moscow State University]]. In the 1970s–1980s A. I. Volpert became one of the leaders of the Russian Mathematical Chemistry scientific community.<ref>{{harvtxt|Manelis|Aldoshin|2005|pp=7–8}} detail briefly Vol'pert's and other scientists contribution to the development of mathematical chemistry. Precisely, they write that "''В работах математического отдел института ( А. Я. Повзнер, А. И. Вольперт, А. Я. Дубовицкий) получили широкое развитие математической основи химической физики: теория систем дифференциальных уравнений, методы оптимизации, современные вычислительные методы методы отображения и т.д., которые легли в основу  современной химической физики (теоретические основы химической кинетики, макрокинетики, теории горения и взрыва и т.д.)''", i.e. (English translation) "''In the Mathematical Department of the Institute ([[Aleksandr Yakovlevich Povzner|A. Ya. Povzner]], A. I. Vol'pert, A. Ya. Dubovitskii) the mathematical foundations of chemical physics have been widely developed: particularly the theory of systems of differential equations, optimization techniques, advanced computational methods, imaging techniques, etc. which formed the basis of modern chemical physics (the theoretical foundations of chemical kinetics, macrokinetics, the theory of combustion and explosion, etc.)''".</ref> He finally joined [[Technion]]’s Faculty of Mathematics in 1993,<ref name="tecbio"/> doing his [[Aliyah]] in 1994.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Ingbar|2010|p=80}}.</ref>

== Work ==

===Index theory and elliptic boundary problems===
Vol'pert developed an effective [[algorithm]] for calculating the index of an elliptic problem before the [[Atiyah-Singer index theorem]] appeared:<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Chuyko|2009|p=79}}. See also {{harvtxt|Mikhlin|1965|pp=185 and 207–208}} and {{harvnb|Mikhlin|Prössdorf|1986|p=369}}.</ref> He was also the first to show that the index of a singular matrix operator can be different from zero.<ref>See {{harvnb|Mikhlin|Prössdorf|1986|p=369}} and also {{harvnb|Prössdorf|1991|p=108}}.</ref>

===Functions of bounded variation===
He was one of the leading contributors to the theory of [[Bounded variation|''BV''-functions]]: he introduced the concept of [[functional superposition]], which enabled him to construct a calculus for such functions and applying it in the theory of [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>In the paper {{Harv|Vol'pert|1967|pp=246–247}}: see also the book {{Harv|Hudjaev|Vol'pert|1985|loc=Chapter 4, §6. "Differentiation formulas"}}.</ref> Precisely, given a [[continuously differentiable function]] <math>f:\mathbb{R}^p \to \mathbb{R}</math> and a function of [[bounded variation]] <math>\boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol x)= (u_1(\boldsymbol{x}), \ldots , u_p(\boldsymbol{x}))</math> with <math>\boldsymbol{x}\in \Bbb R^n</math> and <math>n\ge 1</math>, he proves that <math>f\circ \boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol{x}) = f(\boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol{x}))</math> is again a function of bounded variation and the following [[chain rule]] [[formula]] holds:<ref>See the entry on [[Bounded variation|functions of bounded variation]] for more details on the quantities appearing in this formula: here it is only worth to remark that a more general one, meaningful even for [[lipschitz continuity|Lipschitz continuous functions]] <math>f:\Bbb R^p\to \Bbb R^s</math>, has been proved by [[Luigi Ambrosio]] and [[Gianni Dal Maso]] in the paper {{Harv|Ambrosio|Dal Maso|1990}}.</ref>

:<math>\frac{\partial f(\boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol{x}))}{\partial x_i}=\sum_{k=1}^p\frac{\partial\bar{f}(\boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol{x}))}{\partial u_k}\frac{\partial{u_k(\boldsymbol{x})}}{\partial x_i}
\qquad\forall i=1,\ldots,n</math>

where <math>{\bar f}(\boldsymbol{u}(\boldsymbol{x}))</math> is the already cited functional superposition of  <math>f</math> and <math>\boldsymbol u</math>. By using his results, it is easy to prove that functions of bounded variation form an [[Algebra (ring theory)|algebra]] of [[discontinuous function]]s: in particular, using his calculus for <math>n=1</math>, it is possible to define the product <math>H\cdot \delta</math> of the [[Heaviside step function]] <math>H(x)</math> and the [[Dirac distribution]] <math>\delta(x)</math> in one [[Variable (mathematics)|variable]].<ref>See {{harvtxt|Dal Maso|Lefloch|Murat|1995|pp=483–484}}. This paper is one of several works where the results of the paper {{Harv|Vol'pert|1967|pp=246–247}} are extended in order to define a particular [[Generalized function#Multiplication of distributions|product of distributions]]: the product introduced is called the "''[[Nonconservative product]]''".</ref>

===Chemical kinetics===

His work on chemical kinetics and [[chemical engineering]] led him to define and study [[differential equation on a graph|differential equations on graphs]].<ref>See {{Harv|Vol'pert|1972}} and also {{Harv|Hudjaev|Vol'pert|1985|pp=607–666}}.</ref>

The "''Mathematics in the [[USSR]] 1958–1967''" is a two–volume continuation of the opus "''Mathematics in the [[USSR]] during its first forty years 1917–1957''" and describes the developments of Soviet mathematics during the period 1958–1967. Precisely it is meant as a continuation of the second volume of that work and, as such, is titled "''Biobibliography''" (evidently an [[acronym]] of [[biography]] and [[bibliography]]). It includes new biographies (when possible, brief and complete) and bibliographies of works published by new Soviet mathematicians during that period, and updates on the work and biographies of scientist included in the former volume, alphabetically ordered with respect to author's surname.
